title: Presence in two adult worm maps gave no clear evoked-response prediction gain in 1397 selected pairs
abstract: We tested whether chemical connections found in both adult Witvliet maps D7 and D8 predict response detection in the Randi wild-type atlas. The sample had 1397 directed pairs with a chemical connection in at least one map. Models controlled mean chemical count, electrical count, reverse chemical count, observation count and cell identity. Five folds held out stimulated cells. Adding presence in both maps changed log loss from 0.277920 to 0.278525. The reduction was -0.000604, with a conditional 95% crossed cell bootstrap interval from -0.003460 to 0.002444. Five planned sensitivity checks also had intervals that included zero. Detection rates were 8.16% for one-map edges and 8.42% for two-map edges. Only 545 pairs had exact mean counts represented in both support groups. Two anatomy samples, unequal coverage, different animals, a detection threshold and limited weight overlap prevent a general claim about stable wiring or functional reliability.

display.caption: Left: response detection by mean count and adult map support. Labels give pair counts. Rates are not adjusted. Right: log-loss reduction from adding support. Positive values mean better predictions. Bars are conditional 95% crossed cell bootstrap intervals. All include zero.
